- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is trending up.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >+2% across 3–5 days), consider mean reversion bias — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture short-term reversals; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to recent sentiment swings; apply lagged sentiment smoothing (e.g., 3-day moving average of sentiment) to dampen overfitting.
